newsitem.title: CHINA: China opens home of nuclear bomb to tourists.
newsitem.headline: China opens home of nuclear bomb to tourists.

text.p: China's far-western Qinghai region has opened the birthplace of China's nuclear arsenal to tourists but foreigners are not welcome yet, state media and local officials said on Wednesday.
The former "Nuclear City", located in grasslands 100 km (60 miles) from the Qinghai capital Xining, had been listed as a destination for package tours available in the region, the China Daily said.

The city, once the weapons research centre where China's first atomic and nuclear weapons were developed, had gone through strict environmental testing since it was closed in 1987, the newspaper said.
An official of the Qinghai foreign affairs office said that while Chinese tourists could be permitted to visit the city, now a local government centre, foreigners were still barred.
"We have always wanted to open this area (to foreigners) but... there are necessary formalities," the official said by telephone from Xining.
"There is a plan to open the area but so far it has not been approved," she said.

China carried out its first nuclear test in 1964 at a desert test site in the neighbouring Xinjiang region. Last year Beijing joined other nuclear powers in announcing an indefinite moratorium on further tests.
